title: Automatically tracking neurons in a moving and deforming brain
demonstrated: Non-rigid reference-volume correspondence and time-independent identity clustering in moving adult worms.
implication: Deformation correction, reference anchors, and neuron tracking are prior art; dual-anchor geometry alone is not a first-use claim.
anchoring: Multiple reference volumes sampled throughout recording.
deformation: Straightening, non-rigid registration, and thin-plate-spline correction.
future_frame_access: Whole-recording reference construction and clustering; not a fixed-lag online method.
hypothesis_retention: Registration feature vectors and clusters, not a retained temporal assignment bank.
annotation_requirements: Automated pipeline; human/reference comparisons used for evaluation.
evaluation_scope: Adult freely moving worms; image-derived detection and longitudinal tracking.

title: Fast deep neural correspondence for tracking and identifying neurons in C. elegans using semi-synthetic training
demonstrated: Learned point-cloud correspondence from semi-synthetic training, including temporal neuron matching.
implication: Pairwise learned correspondence is an important baseline, not a full retained temporal identity posterior.
anchoring: Template point cloud paired with a target point cloud.
deformation: Semi-synthetic deformation during training; learned correspondence.
future_frame_access: Pairwise inference; temporal information access depends on chosen template schedule.
hypothesis_retention: Correspondence scores; no maintained temporal assignment bank demonstrated.
annotation_requirements: Semi-synthetic correspondence training; labeled evaluation matches.
evaluation_scope: Neuron tracking and cross-animal identification, including NeRVE recordings.

title: Versatile multiple object tracking in sparse 2D/3D videos via deformable image registration
demonstrated: Annotation-guided deformable image registration, spring constraints, and reference-frame selection in moving worms.
implication: Reference constraints and deformable multi-object tracking are established; sparse manually verified keypoints must not be described as all-frame manual labels for every neuron.
anchoring: Annotated reference frames plus optional partial annotations.
deformation: Local image registration with inter-keypoint spring constraints.
future_frame_access: Reference selection and registration order can use the recording; not a matched fixed-lag online claim.
hypothesis_retention: Optimization of keypoint positions, not a discrete temporal assignment beam.
annotation_requirements: Manual reference annotations; optional verified partial tracks.
evaluation_scope: Sparse keypoints in 2D/3D videos, including freely moving adult worms.

title: 3DeeCellTracker, a deep learning-based pipeline for segmenting and tracking cells in 3D time lapse images
demonstrated: Segmentation, feedforward correspondence, PR-GLS, initial manual correction, and ensemble reference tracking.
implication: Multiple references and neural-cell tracking predate this project. KK outputs generated by this method require documented expert correction before serving as a reference for that same method.
anchoring: Initial corrected segmentation; previous/reference volumes in ensemble mode.
deformation: Feedforward correspondence and PR-GLS point-set transformation.
future_frame_access: Sequential reference tracking; exact look-ahead restriction not established in this review.
hypothesis_retention: Ensemble reference estimates, not a scored temporal assignment beam.
annotation_requirements: Initial corrected labels and segmentation training; subsequent checking differs by dataset.
evaluation_scope: Worm neurons and other 3D cell recordings; detects and tracks cells.

title: Automated neuron tracking inside moving and deforming C. elegans using deep learning and targeted augmentation
demonstrated: Targeted augmentation supplies synthetic annotations for learned 3D neuron segmentation and tracking.
implication: Volumetric shape exploitation is prior art; this does not itself establish a dynamic random-matrix extent posterior.
deformation: Targeted augmentation and learned image segmentation.
future_frame_access: Recording-wide training-frame selection; no matched fixed-lag restriction established.
hypothesis_retention: Learned segmentation/identity predictions, not an explicit temporal assignment bank.
annotation_requirements: Few manual annotations followed by augmentation and optional proofreading.
evaluation_scope: 3D adult-worm neuron tracking with point or volumetric annotations.

title: Deep neural networks to register and annotate cells in moving and deforming nervous systems
demonstrated: Learned dense non-rigid image registration and neuron correspondence in freely moving adult worms.
implication: Registration and ROI linkage accuracy must not be compared to this project's initialized-cohort score without matched data and definitions.
anchoring: Fixed/moving image pairs and downstream ROI linkage.
deformation: Learned dense displacement fields after rigid alignment.
future_frame_access: Image-pair registration and pipeline-level clustering; fixed-lag access not established.
hypothesis_retention: Similarity-based ROI linkage; no discrete temporal history bank demonstrated.
annotation_requirements: Matched centroid supervision and registration training data.
evaluation_scope: Freely moving adult worms and transfer to jellyfish; registration/linking metrics.

title: Multiple Hypothesis Hypergraph Tracking for Posture Identification in Embryonic Caenorhabditis elegans
demonstrated: Ranked-assignment trees with depth-first look-ahead search and a K-best retained-hypothesis alternative; correlated seam-cell motion.
implication: Sections 1.3 and 4.1.3 directly precede rolling-tree versus bounded-beam comparisons; neither search mechanism is new here.
hypothesis_retention: Exponential admitted tree or K-best retained hypotheses.
annotation_requirements: Annotated posture data for learned models and evaluation.
evaluation_scope: Embryonic seam cells, not adult whole-brain neurons.
version: arXiv method manuscript v2, 2022-07-09; not labeled a separate peer-reviewed method paper.

title: Tracking calcium dynamics from individual neurons in behaving animals
demonstrated: eMHT tracklets, thin-plate-spline elastic motion correction, and global gap concatenation in Hydra and mouse imaging.
implication: Combining biological MHT, deformation correction, and gap closing is prior art; a distinct posterior or empirical benefit must be shown.
anchoring: Tracklet endpoints and detected-neuron displacement correspondences.
deformation: Thin-plate-spline elastic field estimated from tracklets.
future_frame_access: Multiframe eMHT and forward/backward global tracklet concatenation.
hypothesis_retention: eMHT alternatives within tracklets; stitching is a separate optimization.
annotation_requirements: Spot detection plus manually validated tracks for evaluation.
evaluation_scope: Behaving Hydra and mouse calcium imaging; variable visibility and gap closing.

title: How To Make Your Cell Tracker Say I dunno!
demonstrated: Assignment alternatives and post-hoc calibrated uncertainty for several linear-assignment cell trackers.
implication: Cell-tracking uncertainty and calibration are established; library use or multiple hypotheses alone cannot support novelty or calibration claims.
anchoring: Generic frame-pair tracking costs supplied by underlying tracker.
deformation: Depends on underlying tracker; no specific worm deformation model.
future_frame_access: Frame-pair uncertainty model; input tracker may use additional context.
hypothesis_retention: Assignment alternatives for marginal uncertainty, not a persistent multiframe history bank.
annotation_requirements: Tracking labels for calibration/evaluation; underlying tracker may need training.
evaluation_scope: Cell-tracking uncertainty across multiple linear-assignment trackers.

title: WormID-Bench, A Benchmark for Whole-Brain Activity Extraction in C. elegans
demonstrated: Multilaboratory detection, semantic identification, and temporal tracking benchmark; point-reference tracking evaluation uses DET/TRA.
implication: Resource reuse is not an independent dataset contribution; initialized-cohort identity accuracy is not directly comparable to end-to-end DET/TRA.
anchoring: Baseline-dependent; this is a benchmark rather than one anchoring mechanism.
deformation: Varying recorded worm motion and baseline-dependent registration.
future_frame_access: Baseline-dependent; no universal matched fixed-lag rule established.
hypothesis_retention: Baseline-dependent; no new posterior mechanism claimed.
annotation_requirements: Curated community point references; asset-level temporal verification must be checked separately.
evaluation_scope: 118 source worms; temporal tracking subset reported as 36 videos, distinct from structural identification samples.
inspected: Version-4 citation metadata and previously retrieved local primary text work/notes/wormid_bench.txt; current publisher-page retrieval was unavailable.
